name: Empire State Building
headline: heightToTip
description: The Empire State Building is a 102-storey skyscraper in Manhattan, New York City, completed in 1931 after about 13 months of construction. CTBUH puts its architectural top at 381 m (1,250 ft), and the spire and broadcast antenna take it to 443.2 m (1,454 ft).

measures.label: Height to tip
measures.note: CTBUH height to tip, including the antenna (1,454 ft)

measures.label: Height (architectural)
measures.note: CTBUH height to architectural top (1,250 ft); the owners give 1,250 ft as the height to the roof of the 102nd floor

facts.text: The building's owners give its height as 1,454 feet (443 meters) including the spire and antenna, and 1,250 feet to the roof of the 102nd floor.
It has 102 floors above ground and 1 below ground.
The building weighs 365,000 tons, according to its official site.
The 86th-floor observatory is 1,050 feet (320 meters) above the ground.
It was completed in 1931 after 13 months (410 days) of construction.

sources.publisher: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (The Skyscraper Center)
sources.title: Empire State Building - The Skyscraper Center

sources.publisher: Empire State Realty Trust (Empire State Building official site)
sources.title: Empire State Building Facts & Figures

caveats: The official ESB page converts 1,250 ft to 380 m in one sentence and to 381 m in another; CTBUH gives 381 m. The CTBUH metric values are used for the measures. The two sources agree on 1,454 ft to the tip and 1,250 ft to the roof.
The official site gives the weight as '365,000 tons' without saying whether these are short or metric tons, so it is recorded only as a fact.
